title: Why Counting Rhythms Doesn't Teach Rhythm (And What Actually Works)

method.teacher_system: The teacher critiques traditional counting-based rhythm instruction and explains why it fails beginners. He introduces the concept of rhythmic audiation through somatic feel and movement. Finally, he advocates for anchoring macro-beats and micro-beats in bodily weight and balance before adding conceptual theory.
method.signature: Explaining rhythm pedagogy through bodily weight, balance, and vestibular processing rather than standard notation or numbers

practices.what: Demonstrates the cadence of a 3/4 rhythm by speaking the subdivisions aloud with emphasis on the beat.
Shows how to physically tap and feel the macro beat on the first count rather than accenting every quarter note.

beliefs.belief: Counting rhythms is not an effective way to learn how to audiate rhythm for beginners.
Rhythm is processed through the part of the brain that controls balance and vestibular systems.

struggles.theme: Counting makes playing feel jerky and mechanical rather than flowing
Struggled with counting or reading music notation for years
Counting gets in the way of listening to the actual music

clicked.theme: Realizing rhythm is physical and felt in the body, not mental
Connecting movement and dance experience to playing instruments

meant.theme: Validated decades of teaching experience or personal learning struggles

method.limits: The video is a lecture-style discussion by a single teacher sitting in a chair, with no physical dance demonstration or student interaction shown.
